faq.q1: How can I book an appointment?
faq.a1: You can contact us by phone at +30 2310 545 261, by email at iopapaio@gmail.com, or by filling out the contact form on the website. We will respond within 24 hours to schedule a meeting.
faq.q2: What areas of law do you specialize in?

faq.a3: Yes, we handle cases throughout Greece. For cases outside Thessaloniki, collaboration with a local lawyer or additional travel expenses may be required, agreed upon in advance.

faq.a4: The duration depends on the type of case, jurisdiction and court schedules. At our first meeting we will provide a realistic time estimate based on our experience with similar cases.

faq.a5: Absolutely. We are bound by professional confidentiality as provided by the Greek Code of Lawyers. Any information you share with us — whether in meetings, by email or by phone — remains strictly confidential.
faq.q6: Can I contact you by email for updates?
faq.a6: Of course. We provide continuous updates on the progress of your case via email, phone or in-person meetings, according to your preferences.

about.bio1: With more than 25 years in banking law and enforcement proceedings, we defend borrowers, individuals and businesses against banks, funds and debt management companies. We do not accept an auction, a seizure or a payment order as a fait accompli — every file is examined from the start.

bioParagraphs: Ioannis Papaioannou is an Attorney at the Supreme Court of Greece (Areios Pagos), with extensive courtroom experience in civil, commercial and banking law. He has maintained a law office in Thessaloniki since 2000, handling cases of significant legal and economic importance for individuals, professionals and businesses.

Born in Preveza and raised in Munich, he holds a law degree from the Democritus University of Thrace and an LL.M. from Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München. His legal career combines Greek courtroom practice with a German legal education — a combination that shapes his approach to complex cases: precise, methodical and strategically minded.

In recent years he has concentrated a significant part of his practice on banking law cases, enforcement proceedings, foreclosure auctions, objections against payment orders and disputes with funds and debt management companies. His practice is not limited to passive defence of the borrower, but includes a full review of the claim, its legitimacy, the enforcement acts, interest charges, fees and the chain of debt transfer.

Particular emphasis is placed on protecting the home and assets of debtors facing payment orders, seizures and foreclosure auctions. His approach combines judicial defence with substantive negotiation — aiming not merely at temporary relief from pressure, but at a genuine strategic solution.

He also heads the legal team of the Association of Borrowers and Consumer Protection of Northern Greece, actively supporting borrowers and consumers facing over-indebtedness, bank claims and enforcement proceedings. This role reflects his consistent engagement with debtor protection issues and his conviction that legal support against banks, funds and debt management companies must be immediate, well-documented and assertive.

His legal philosophy is built on careful study of each case file, timely use of procedural options and a realistic but determined approach. Every payment order, every seizure and every foreclosure auction is treated not as a fait accompli, but as an act that must be rigorously examined — legally and factually.

The office's goal is to provide substantive legal protection, with clarity, honesty and a focus on results. Every case begins with a full assessment of the facts, documents, deadlines and options for defence or negotiation, so that the client knows from the outset what their actual position is and what steps need to be taken.

alpha.seoTitle: Alpha Bank Lawyer – Loans & Foreclosures in Thessaloniki
alpha.seoDescription: Is Alpha Bank or the servicer handling your loan pressing you with a payment order or auction? Every document has a defence deadline. Objection, suspension, settlement with a haircut in Thessaloniki. Tel: +30 2310 545 261.
alpha.heroTitle: Lawyer for Alpha Bank loans and foreclosures in Thessaloniki and across Greece
alpha.intro: If you have a non-performing Alpha Bank loan, or you have received an extrajudicial notice, termination of the contract, a payment order, a writ of execution, a seizure report or an auction programme, your case is no longer at a theoretical stage. In some cases the claim is still pursued by Alpha Bank itself. In others, the loan has been transferred to a special purpose vehicle (fund) and management has been assigned to a credit servicing company (servicer). The first thing we check is exactly that: who is pursuing you today and with what legal standing. Ioannis Papaioannou, Legal Advisor to the Association of Borrowers and Consumer Protection of Northern Greece, has been defending borrowers against banks and servicers for more than 25 years. We know how Alpha Bank works in practice, which documents must be produced, and which points of the case must be checked before the borrower is pushed into a settlement out of fear or into an auction without a real defence.
alpha.whatTitle: Alpha Bank, funds and servicers: who really pursues your loan
alpha.whatText: An Alpha Bank loan may today be in different hands than when it was signed. Sometimes it remains with the bank and sometimes it has been transferred, through securitisation, to a special purpose vehicle (fund), with management assigned to a servicer. This matters in practice. In every case we must check who is the real beneficiary of the claim today, when and how the loan was transferred from Alpha Bank, with which documents the transfer and the servicing assignment are proven, whether the party enforcing has legal standing in the specific procedure, and whether the amount demanded arises in a lawful, clear and verifiable way. A document, whether from Alpha Bank or from a servicer, does not mean everything is settled. It means the case must be checked immediately. Before any discussion of a settlement, we must know what is demanded, by whom, with what standing and with what calculation. If management has been taken over by a specific company, such as Cepal, doValue, Intrum or QQuant, see our dedicated page on it too.
alpha.protectTitle: Protecting your home from a foreclosure on an Alpha Bank loan
alpha.protectText: No property is lost because a letter arrived. It is at risk when the case is not checked in time and the lawful means of defence are left unused. From the termination of the contract to the payment order, the writ of execution, the seizure and the auction, each stage has its own significance. We examine whether there is room for an objection, an application for suspension, inclusion in the out-of-court mechanism, direct negotiation or another targeted action. We treat no auction as a foregone conclusion. From the outset we check the legal standing of the party enforcing, the transfer of the claim from Alpha Bank, the amount of the debt, the interest, the charges, the abusive terms and every act of enforcement. There, in the details that are often not checked, the course of a case can change. The aim is not simply to move fast. The aim is to move correctly, before enforcement appears to be the only road.
alpha.deadlinesTitle: I received an extrajudicial notice, payment order or seizure on an Alpha Bank loan: the deadlines you must not miss
alpha.deadlinesIntro: Not every document has the same legal weight. The termination of the contract is one thing, the payment order another and the seizure yet another. But each stage shows the case is moving and the time to react is shrinking.

deadlines.title: Termination of contract / extrajudicial notice
deadlines.desc: Termination of the loan contract is usually the first serious move. The debt now appears as due and payable and the road opens to a payment order. At this stage there may not yet be an objection deadline, but there is time that must not be wasted. The case must be checked before the claim becomes a judicial title.

deadlines.title: Payment order
deadlines.desc: The payment order is the next step. The claim takes judicial form and can lead to enforcement. An objection to the payment order is filed within fifteen working days of its service, when the debtor has a residence or seat in Greece. If the residence or seat is abroad or unknown, the deadline is thirty working days.

deadlines.title: Seizure
deadlines.desc: Seizure is the stage at which enforcement has already begun and, for real estate, an auction is already set. An objection to enforcement, on grounds concerning the claim, the writ, the procedure and the seizure, is filed within forty-five days of the seizure. If a suspension of the auction is also needed, that move is examined separately and must be made in good time.

alpha.deadlinesWarning: None of these deadlines is extended because the borrower needed time to recover from the shock. That is why the file should be reviewed the moment the first document arrives, not when the auction is already close.
alpha.cta1Title: Do you have an Alpha Bank or servicer document in front of you?
alpha.cta1Text: An immediate first assessment: what was served on you, which deadline is running, which moves are available. Call +30 2310 545 261 or send the form.
alpha.negotiationTitle: Negotiation strategy for Alpha Bank loans: a settlement aiming at a debt write-off (haircut), where the case allows it
alpha.negotiationIntro: Whether you are facing Alpha Bank or the servicer managing the claim, you do not go to ask for mercy. You go to present a position. Whichever side knows the case better holds the stronger negotiating advantage. Our job is to pass that advantage to the borrower. Before any contact we check the legal standing of the party pursuing, the real beneficiary of the claim, the transfer from Alpha Bank, the balance, the interest, the charges and every element affecting the amount. An amount that has not been verified must not become the starting point of a negotiation.
negotiationPoints: The settlement must withstand time. A deal that looks good on paper but collapses on the second or third instalment is worthless. The proposal must be linked to the borrower's real financial capacity, the value of the security, the course of the claim and the data of the case.
A debt write-off (haircut) is not asked for as a wish; it is documented as a negotiating goal when the elements of the case allow it.

The price at which the fund acquired the loan from Alpha Bank, the history of the portfolio, the prospect of recovery, the value of the property and the existence of a judicial challenge are factors that can change the discussion.

The best negotiation takes place when the borrower has already exercised, or is ready to exercise, their rights. A well-founded objection, an application for suspension or a serious judicial challenge changes the basis of the discussion: the other side knows that, if there is no agreement, the case will be decided in court.
alpha.negotiationOutro: A proposal is not enough to be heard; it has to hold. That means a settlement that can actually be paid, a write-off where it is documented, and judicial pressure where it is needed. Against a bank or a servicer, no one hands you the good terms; they are won through control of the file and proper preparation.
alpha.cta2Title: Before you reply to or sign anything with Alpha Bank or the servicer, talk to us first.
alpha.cta2Text: Many Alpha Bank loans were transferred through securitisations, and the chain of transfer is often the weakest point of the other side. A hasty acknowledgment of debt can close doors that are open today. First the check, then the answer.
alpha.anakopiTitle: Objection and Suspension of Auction before the Courts of Thessaloniki and across Greece
alpha.anakopiText1:
Enforcement is not met with general protests, but with a targeted procedural review of every act, every document and every amount invoked by the pursuing side.

Our Law Office handles, on a daily basis, cases of objections, applications for suspension and auctions before the Courts of Thessaloniki and across Greek territory.

In every case we fully review the writ of payment, the seizure report, the documents of transfer of the claim, the servicing assignment, the analysis of the debt, the interest, the charges, the services and compliance with the lawful deadlines. An objection must not be a routine defence pleading. It must be procedurally precise, evidentially documented and adapted to the actual data of the specific file.
alpha.anakopiText2:
Where required, the objection is accompanied by an application for suspension, aiming to temporarily avert the auction until the substance of the dispute is judged. Suspension is not merely a means of delay. It is a procedural tool of protection, when there is a serious ground to annul the enforcement and a risk of irreparable harm from the immediate conduct of the auction.

Our goal is the immediate and full assessment of the file, the highlighting of the substantive and procedural defects, and the formation of a concrete strategy either to overturn the enforcement in court or to create a strong negotiating position against the bank, the claims acquisition company or the credit servicing company.

In auction cases, time is critical. The timely submission of documents and the immediate legal review can determine whether there is real room for objection, suspension or an out-of-court settlement.
alpha.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions about Alpha Bank loans

faq.q: My loan was with Alpha Bank but now another company is calling me. What does this mean?
faq.a: It means Alpha Bank probably transferred the claim to a special purpose vehicle (fund) and assigned management to a credit servicing company (servicer), such as, depending on the portfolio, Cepal, doValue, Intrum or QQuant. It does not mean the debt is self-evident or correctly calculated. The transfer, the legal standing and the amount must be checked before you do anything.

faq.q: Can Alpha Bank or the servicer put my property up for auction?
faq.a: Only with an enforceable title and an entirely lawful procedure, and both are reviewed in court. The standing of the party enforcing, the amount of the claim and every act of enforcement have points of challenge with specific deadlines.

faq.q: Is it worth negotiating with Alpha Bank or the servicer on my own?
faq.a: It is dangerous. Across from you stands a specialised mechanism that negotiates thousands of cases, while you have one. Without a file review you do not even know whether the amount demanded is correct, nor what your real negotiating power is.

faq.q: The auction is very close. Is there still hope?
faq.a: It depends on the file, and the answer comes only after we see it, quickly. Procedural defects may provide grounds for action even in the last days. Call immediately at +30 2310 545 261.

faq.q: What documents do you need for the review?
faq.a: Everything you have received from Alpha Bank and from any servicing company: the loan contract, letters, extrajudicial notices, the termination, the payment order, the writ of execution, the seizure report and the auction programme. Most important of all: the dates of service.

The principal, the interest, the payments already made and the additional charges imposed must all emerge clearly.

This review should happen as soon as a special purpose vehicle or a servicing company appears in Eurobank's place, and in any event before a settlement is signed or the stated balance is acknowledged. faq.q: Can an auction be stayed just days before it takes place?

faq.q: What is an objection to enforcement and when do we file it?
faq.a: The objection to enforcement is the main judicial remedy against compulsory enforcement. Through it, the payment writ, the seizure, the auction, the claim, the interest, the charges and the standing of the party pursuing enforcement are all reviewed. The deadlines are strict. In typical cases, the objection is filed within 45 days of the seizure, while special deadlines apply to the final act of enforcement, particularly after the auction. faq.q: Can a fund auction my home?

exodikastikos.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions about the Out-of-Court Mechanism

faq.q: Which debts can I settle through the out-of-court mechanism?
faq.a: Debts to banks and claims-management companies (funds), to the tax authority (AADE), to social-security funds (e.g. e-EFKA) and to municipalities. The key advantage is that all of these can be addressed in a single procedure, instead of separate negotiations with each one. Exactly which of your debts are included and which may be excluded is something we check in the first assessment of the file.

faq.q: What are the conditions for inclusion?
faq.a: Inclusion depends on the profile of the debts, their relationship to your assets and income, and the absence of grounds for exclusion. It is not enough simply to owe money, since your case must meet the criteria of the law and the proposed settlement must be viable. That is why the conditions are checked before submission, so as not to start a procedure that leads to a dead end or an unfavourable proposal.

faq.q: Over how many instalments can I repay?
faq.a: The law provides for repayment over a large number of monthly instalments, with the exact number differing depending on the creditor, with one figure for the State and social-security funds and another for banks and management companies. The final number of instalments and the amount of each one result from the mechanism's calculation based on income, asset value and the level of debt. Our aim is a settlement that genuinely holds over time.

faq.q: Can part of the debt be written off?
faq.a: Yes, in suitable cases a write-off of part of the principal debt, interest and penalties is provided for. The write-off is neither automatic nor guaranteed, as it results from the calculation and from the data of the case. The better documented the file, the stronger your position in pursuing better terms.

faq.q: If I already have a payment order or a scheduled auction, does the out-of-court mechanism protect me?
faq.a: The application may trigger protection against enforcement measures, under conditions, but it does not by itself cancel the defence deadlines already running. If a payment order, seizure or auction is pending, the out-of-court mechanism must be coordinated with an objection or a suspension application. That is why the file is assessed as a whole and immediately, before a deadline becomes a missed opportunity.

exodikastikos.ctaTitle: The out-of-court mechanism is won mainly in the preparation, not in the mere submission of the application.
exodikastikos.ctaText: We check the conditions, the debts and a realistic outcome and tell you honestly what your position is, based on real data rather than promises.

cepal.whatTitle: What Is Cepal and What Does It Mean for Your Loan?
cepal.whatText: Cepal Hellas Financial Services is not a bank and is not the holder of the claim. It is a claim management company that acts on behalf of the entity presented as the holder of the claim — namely a special purpose vehicle that acquired loan claims from banks. This means that in every case it must be examined who the actual holder of the claim is, when and how the loan was transferred, with what documents the transfer is proven, whether Cepal has standing to act in the specific procedure and whether the amount claimed is established in a lawful, clear and verifiable manner. The existence of a document from Cepal does not mean everything is settled. It means the case must be reviewed immediately. Before any settlement is made, we must know what is being claimed, by whom, on what basis of standing and with what calculation.
cepal.protectTitle: Protecting Your Home from a Foreclosure Initiated by Cepal
cepal.protectText: Cepal is one of the claim management companies most frequently seen in enforcement and foreclosure proceedings. In a number of cases its stance appears particularly strict and inflexible, especially when settlement proposals are rejected without a real assessment of the debtor's actual financial circumstances. But that can also be the weak point of the case. An uncompromising stance, when combined with prolonged inaction, refusal of a sustainable settlement, excessive inflation of the debt, incomplete information or enforcement pursued without real weighing of the circumstances, may under certain conditions be used legally — particularly in the context of arguments of abuse of right. In every case we review from the start Cepal's standing, the assignment of the claim, the amount of the debt, the interest, the charges, the abusive terms, the services of process and every act of enforcement. The high volume of cases handled by management companies often leads to standardised moves. It is there, in the details that must not be left unchecked, that real defence can be found. We treat no foreclosure as final. We examine whether there is room for an objection, a suspension application, entry into the out-of-court workout, direct negotiation or another targeted action. The goal is not merely to gain time. The goal is to shift the balance, before enforcement appears as the only road.
cepal.deadlinesTitle: Received a Notice, Payment Order or Seizure from Cepal — The Deadlines That Must Not Be Missed
cepal.deadlinesIntro: Not all documents from Cepal carry the same legal weight. A formal notice terminating the contract is the first serious warning step. A payment order turns the claim into a judicial title. A seizure means enforcement has already begun and, when it concerns real property, an auction is set along with it.

deadlines.title: Formal notice terminating the contract
deadlines.desc: With a formal notice terminating the contract, we do not stay idle. The debt is now presented as overdue and due, and the way to the next move is open. At this stage there may not yet be an objection deadline, but there is time to review the case, to respond formally, to negotiate and to prepare a defence before the claim takes a judicial form.

deadlines.title: Payment order
deadlines.desc: With a payment order, we act immediately. An objection is filed within fifteen working days of its service, when the debtor's residence or seat is in Greece. If the residence or seat is abroad or unknown, the deadline is thirty working days. If this deadline is missed, the debtor's position is decisively weakened.

deadlines.title: Seizure
deadlines.desc: With a seizure, there is no room for half-measures. An objection against enforcement, on grounds concerning the claim, the writ of execution, the preliminary procedure and the seizure itself, is filed within forty-five days from the date of seizure. If a suspension of the auction must also be sought, that step is examined separately and must be taken at the right time.

cepal.deadlinesWarning: Greek law does not wait for the debtor to recover from the shock. Every stage opens a window for action that closes at some point. That is why the case must be reviewed from the start, before enforcement appears as the only road.

cepal.negotiationTitle: Negotiation Strategy with Cepal — Settlement Aimed at Debt Write-Off (Haircut)
cepal.negotiationIntro: You do not approach Cepal to ask for a favour. You approach it to present a position. Whichever side knows the case better holds the negotiating advantage. Our job is to make sure that advantage passes to the debtor. Before any contact we review Cepal's standing, the actual holder of the claim, the assignment, the balance, the interest, the charges and every element that affects the amount. We do not enter a negotiation without knowing exactly what claim we are dealing with. An amount that has not been verified must not become the starting point of a discussion.
negotiationPoints: The settlement must be tailored to actual repayment capacity. The goal is not an agreement that looks good on paper and collapses after a few months. The goal is a settlement that holds up over time, with specific numbers, a specific financial basis and a clear strategy.
On that basis we also build the request for a debt write-off (haircut). Cepal manages claims linked to portfolios acquired at an economic value below the nominal balance.
We do not treat that as theory. We use it in practice, combined with the value of the security, collectability, the history of the claim and the facts of the case.

The best negotiation happens when the debtor has already exercised, or is ready to exercise, their rights. A well-founded objection, a suspension application or a serious judicial challenge works as a negotiating lever. The claim manager realises it is not facing a frightened debtor but a legally represented counterparty.
cepal.negotiationOutro: The goal is not the best possible settlement under pressure. It is the settlement that fits the specific case. With specific numbers, specific arguments and a specific strategy. The best terms are not given. They are won through review, preparation and properly built pressure.
cepal.cta2Title: Before signing anything with Cepal — speak to us first.
cepal.cta2Text: A rushed settlement can be worse than signing nothing. We review first, then decide.
cepal.anakopiTitle: Objection and Suspension of Cepal Auctions in Thessaloniki
cepal.anakopiText1: Cepal's high case volume makes it particularly exposed to procedural defects. Grounds that typically support objections and suspensions in Cepal cases:
anakopiPoints: Weak authority chain: securitisation and management assignment involve multiple transfer steps that must each be properly documented — gaps here are a significant basis for objection.
Incorrect debt amount: unlawful compound interest, abusive fees, miscalculated default interest.
Unfair contractual terms: clauses that were not individually negotiated and that undermine the legal foundation of the claim.
Formal enforcement defects: irregular service of process, incorrect amounts in the seizure report, failure to observe mandatory intervals.
cepal.anakopiText2: Where the case requires it, an objection is accompanied by an immediate suspension application so that the auction is stayed until a court decision is issued. This combination — legal defence and parallel negotiation — is usually the most effective approach.

faq.q: Cepal is asking me to sign an out-of-court settlement. Should I?
faq.a: Do not sign anything without legal review. An out-of-court agreement may block defences you currently have — objection, debt challenge, suspension. We review it carefully before any signature.

faq.q: Cepal manages a high volume of claims. Can I really fight them?
faq.a: High volume does not mean every action is lawful, correct and unassailable. On the contrary, mass claims-management operations frequently produce errors in service of process, debt calculations, authorisation documents, claim transfers and enforcement acts. Those are what we examine first, because that is often where the case is decided.

faq.q: My loan was with Alpha Bank. Why is Cepal writing to me?
faq.a: Because the claim may have been transferred to a loan acquirer — such as Galaxy II — and Cepal may have been appointed to manage it. That does not mean everything was done correctly. We check whether the transfer, the management assignment, the notification and every subsequent act were carried out lawfully. The case is decided on the paperwork, not on the logo.

faq.q: What happens if I simply do not respond to Cepal?
faq.a: Silence is not a defence. If a payment order has been issued or a seizure has taken place, inaction allows Cepal to proceed without obstacle. The earlier you have the file reviewed, the more options remain open.

Enforcement is not met with general protests, but with a targeted procedural review of every act, every document and every amount invoked by the pursuing side.

Our Law Office handles, on a daily basis, cases of objections, applications for suspension and auctions before the Courts of Thessaloniki and across Greek territory.

In every case we fully review the writ of payment, the seizure report, the documents of transfer of the claim, the servicing assignment, the analysis of the debt, the interest, the charges, the services and compliance with the lawful deadlines. An objection must not be a routine defence pleading. It must be procedurally precise, evidentially documented and adapted to the actual data of the specific file.
ethnikiBiz.anakopiText2:
Where required, the objection is accompanied by an application for suspension, aiming to temporarily avert the auction until the substance of the dispute is judged. Suspension is not merely a means of delay. It is a procedural tool of protection, when there is a serious ground to annul the enforcement and a risk of irreparable harm from the immediate conduct of the auction.

Our goal is the immediate and full assessment of the file, the highlighting of the substantive and procedural defects, and the formation of a concrete strategy either to overturn the enforcement in court or to create a strong negotiating position against the bank, the claims acquisition company or the credit servicing company.

In auction cases, time is critical. The timely submission of documents and the immediate legal review can determine whether there is real room for objection, suspension or an out-of-court settlement.
ethnikiBiz.faqTitle: FAQ: Businesses and National Bank of Greece

faq.q: I have personally guaranteed a corporate loan to National Bank of Greece. Is my personal property at risk?
faq.a: A personal guarantee triggers liability, but its extent and validity are checked. We examine the limits of the amount, the terms of the guarantee, any abusive clauses and whether the lawful conditions were met. Not every guarantee is unlimited or untouchable.

faq.q: Can my business account or equipment be seized?
faq.a: With an enforceable title and a lawful procedure, yes, but every act of enforcement (garnishment, freezing of accounts, auction of fixed assets) has points of challenge with specific deadlines. An immediate objection and application for suspension can keep the business standing.

faq.q: My business owes banks, social security and the tax office at once. What happens?
faq.a: Here the out-of-court mechanism for businesses is examined, allowing a single settlement of debts to banks, funds, social security (EFKA) and the tax office, where the conditions are met. We check whether it is preferable to the judicial route.

faq.q: The business has stopped operating. Is a defence still worthwhile?
faq.a: It is, especially to limit personal guarantees and protect the personal property of guarantors and managers. Even if the company closed, the guarantees and debts may follow you personally.

faq.q: What documents do you need for the review?
faq.a: The loan/credit agreement, the guarantee contracts, the security documents, the letters and every document from National Bank of Greece: extrajudicial notices, termination, payment order, seizure report. Most important: the dates of service.

An objection against enforcement, on grounds concerning the claim, the writ of execution, the preliminary procedure and the seizure itself, is filed within forty-five days from the date of seizure. If a suspension of the auction must also be sought, that step is examined separately and at the right time.

qquantBiz.negotiationTitle: Negotiation and settlement of corporate debts, aiming at viability
qquantBiz.negotiationIntro: In a business debt, a settlement is not merely a matter of instalments. It is a matter of viability. Before any contact with the servicer QQuant we check the legal standing, the real balance, the guarantees and the data of the business, so that the proposal rests on numbers that hold. The goal is a settlement served by real cash flow, with a debt write-off (haircut) where documented and a controlled extent of personal guarantees.
negotiationPoints: The amount is cleaned up before it is discussed. In debts that resurface after years, interest, charges and compounding may have inflated the balance significantly. An amount that has not been verified must not become the basis of a settlement.

The settlement must rest on economic reality. A proposal that looks impressive and collapses in a few months has no value. The goal is a settlement that holds, with specific numbers, specific arguments and a clear strategy.

On that basis we also build the request for a debt write-off (haircut). In old portfolios, the distance between the book balance and the real economic value of the claim can create substantial negotiating room. We do not invoke that room in general terms. We document it.

The best negotiation happens when the debtor has already exercised, or is ready to exercise, their rights. A well-founded objection, a suspension application, a serious limitation argument or a documented challenge to standing turns the conversation from a plea into a contest of positions.
qquantBiz.negotiationOutro: For businesses, the best deal is the one that lets the business continue. A settlement that is served, guarantees that are bounded, judicial pressure where needed.
qquantBiz.cta2Title: Before you sign a settlement or acknowledge a corporate debt, talk to us first.
qquantBiz.cta2Text: In business debts, a hasty signature can trigger personal guarantees or acknowledge an amount that could be challenged. First the check, then the answer.
qquantBiz.anakopiTitle: Objection and Suspension of QQuant Enforcement in Thessaloniki
qquantBiz.anakopiText1: At the Thessaloniki courts, where we litigate daily, QQuant cases are decided on the details of the file. The grounds of objection that most often succeed:
anakopiPoints: Limitation of the claim or part of it: in loans terminated years ago, time has often done its work — it just needs to be raised properly.
Authority defects: the multiple transfers of portfolios that ended up with QQuant must be fully proven — a missing link means a well-founded ground of objection.
Incorrect debt amount: unlawful compounding, abusive charges and interest that does not withstand judicial scrutiny.
Procedural defects: irregular service, errors in the seizure report, failure to observe statutory deadlines and formalities.
qquantBiz.anakopiText2: Where the case requires it, the objection is combined with a suspension application so that no enforcement act proceeds before the merits are decided. In parallel, the pending case serves as leverage for a realistic settlement.

faq.q: I have personally guaranteed a corporate loan to the servicer QQuant. Is my personal property at risk?
faq.a: A personal guarantee triggers liability, but its extent and validity are checked. We examine the limits of the amount, the terms of the guarantee, any abusive clauses and whether the lawful conditions were met. Not every guarantee is unlimited or untouchable.

faq.q: Can my business account or equipment be seized?
faq.a: With an enforceable title and a lawful procedure, yes, but every act of enforcement (garnishment, freezing of accounts, auction of fixed assets) has points of challenge with specific deadlines. An immediate objection and application for suspension can keep the business standing.

faq.q: My business owes banks, social security and the tax office at once. What happens?
faq.a: Here the out-of-court mechanism for businesses is examined, allowing a single settlement of debts to banks, funds, social security (EFKA) and the tax office, where the conditions are met. We check whether it is preferable to the judicial route.

faq.q: The business has stopped operating. Is a defence still worthwhile?
faq.a: It is, especially to limit personal guarantees and protect the personal property of guarantors and managers. Even if the company closed, the guarantees and debts may follow you personally.

faq.q: What documents do you need for the review?
faq.a: The loan/credit agreement, the guarantee contracts, the security documents, the letters and every document from the servicer QQuant: extrajudicial notices, termination, payment order, seizure report. Most important: the dates of service.
